intro: The AI world is reeling today after Jensen Huang's sudden resignation from Nvidia, capping a scandal that has spiraled from tabloid shock into a full-blown national security crisis involving alleged Chinese intelligence ties and GPU smuggling — and the political fallout is still spreading. But the industry isn't standing still: Google dropped Gemini 4 Hydrogen as its new speed-first model across Search and its entire product ecosystem, ElevenLabs unveiled a team-oriented AI meeting app, and The Verge gave Anthropic's new Claude Duet agent a verdict of "surprisingly helpful but occasionally neurotic." It's one of those days where the biggest story in AI isn't about a model launch — it's about the man who made the GPUs they all run on walking out the door.

stories.title: Jensen Huang resigns from Nvidia as scandal widens into national security and political crisis
stories.summary: Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO and board member effective immediately after 33 years, following NYT reports linking him to extramarital affairs including one with an alleged Chinese intelligence asset connected to Megaspeed, a Singaporean firm under investigation for smuggling GPUs to China. CFO Colette Kress was named interim CEO. The fallout is spreading: US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick faces potential dismissal over alleged inaction on the spy scandal; House committee chairs are seeking a closed-door briefing from Huang on national security concerns; and a WSJ report revealed Huang had privately described Kress as 'a deer in the headlights.' Separately, MIT Technology Review reported that Nvidia privately confirmed to Congress it could implement chip-tracking anti-smuggling measures even as the Semiconductor Industry Association publicly called them 'potentially infeasible.' Israeli VCs, noting Nvidia's 6,000 employees and largest non-US R&D facility in Israel, see Huang's departure as unlikely to kill demand but believe it could open a window for AI chip competitors.
stories.opinion: The resignation confirms that the board pressure reported yesterday has culminated in an immediate leadership change. The widening scandal now threatens not just Nvidia's stability but US trade enforcement credibility, with the chip-tracking revelation suggesting the industry actively lobbied against feasible security measures. Whether interim CEO Kress can steady the ship—especially given Huang's reported lack of confidence in her—will be tested when Nvidia reports earnings on November 17. Where coverage differs: The Rundown AI reports Nvidia stock dropped 'over 14%' while yesterday's coverage cited '$427 billion' in lost market value WSJ (via TechCrunch) reports Huang called Kress 'a deer in the headlights' while The Rundown AI and The Verge present her appointment neutrally TechCrunch reports a third affair was later reported by Reuters; The Rundown AI mentions 'multiple reports of relationships with employees' without specifying a third The Verge frames the story primarily around Nvidia's China business dealings; Guardian frames it around the spy scandal and Lutnick's political jeopardy TechCrunch reports Kress had scaled back Nvidia's OpenAI Ohio data center commitment from $250 billion to $105 billion; other sources do not mention this

stories.title: Google launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a speed-optimized AI model across its product ecosystem
stories.summary: Google DeepMind announced Gemini 4 Hydrogen on November 12, 2026, a new model in the Gemini 4 family optimized for speed and efficiency in coding, agentic workflows, and complex queries. While the frontier models Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Argon handle deep reasoning, Hydrogen is designed for rapid execution and is now the default model in Google's AI Mode for Search. It is available across Google AI Studio, the Gemini API, the Gemini app, Google Search, Google Antigravity, and paid Google AI Pro/Ultra subscribers. Google claims it surpasses Argon on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at its default high thinking level, and offers new thinking level options including 'xhigh' mode. Google's VP of Search product Robby Stein calls it 'the biggest model upgrade to Search yet.'
stories.opinion: Google is positioning Hydrogen as the workhorse model that brings Gemini 4-level intelligence to everyday tasks and all user tiers, while reserving Carbon and Argon for frontier reasoning. Making it the default in Search signals confidence and directly challenges competitors' consumer-facing models. Where coverage differs: DeepMind Blog emphasizes coding and agentic workflow optimization; The Verge emphasizes improved handling of complex queries with typos and multiple parts The Verge mentions availability on 'Google Antigravity' which is not mentioned in the DeepMind Blog post

stories.title: ElevenLabs launches ElevenAI, a team-oriented meeting and dictation app with agent integration
stories.summary: ElevenLabs released an experimental app called ElevenAI that combines meeting note-taking, dictation in 90+ languages, and agent integration for teams and enterprises. Announced at the company's 11/11 Summit in New York, the app is in preview with early access sign-ups. The $22 billion-valued company positions ElevenAI as a team-oriented product entering a space occupied by Fireflies, Wispr Flow, and Granola.
stories.opinion: ElevenLabs is expanding beyond its voice AI roots into the crowded meeting-productivity space, betting that agent integration and multilingual dictation can differentiate it from established competitors.

stories.title: Research finds datacenter industry uses propaganda to suppress community opposition
stories.summary: Research findings indicate the datacenter industry employs propaganda, disinformation, and information control tactics to shape public opinion and suppress community opposition to datacenter construction. Critics have been labeled 'Antifa,' 'commies,' and 'Chinese bots' by tech leaders and politicians, who characterize resistance as a 'documented psyop.' The authors argue big tech uses misdirection and technical jargon to obscure potential harms to local communities.
stories.opinion: The piece highlights a growing tension between the AI infrastructure buildout and affected communities, suggesting the industry's response to legitimate local concerns has been to delegitimize opposition rather than address it.

stories.title: Pew finds large majorities say social media companies and news orgs hold too much political power
stories.summary: A Pew Research Center analysis finds 69% of U.S. adults believe social media companies have too much influence in politics, while 55% say the same about news organizations. Only 6% and 14% respectively think these institutions have too little influence. The newsletter also covers Mississippi electing its first Democratic U.S. Senator in 44 years (Scott Colom) and the shutdown of Salon after 30+ years.
stories.opinion: The findings reflect broad bipartisan skepticism toward institutional media power, though the survey does not distinguish between concern about platform algorithms and concern about editorial decisions.

stories.title: The Verge reviews Claude Duet: surprisingly helpful but occasionally neurotic
stories.summary: The Verge's Allison Johnson reviews Claude Duet, Anthropic's new consumer-facing AI agent for professionals and small business owners. Available as a research preview to Pro, Max, and Ultra subscribers in the US, Duet gets its own app and is designed to manage work and travel schedules using its own judgment about what needs attention. Johnson finds it genuinely useful but notes it can be overly eager and somewhat neurotic, occasionally acting like a nag.
stories.opinion: Duet enters a growing field of consumer AI agents alongside Meta's Muse and OpenAI's Dots, positioning itself as work-focused rather than a general lifestyle assistant. The 'neurotic' observation suggests Anthropic's safety-conscious design philosophy may create a distinctive but polarizing user experience.

stories.title: First Dog on the Moon introduces Pino, an AI-powered virtual kiwi who likes trains and cats
stories.summary: A cartoon by First Dog on the Moon introduces Pino, an autonomous virtual kiwi powered by AI who independently decides he is into trains and cats. The piece is a humorous take on finding a valid use case for artificial intelligence.
stories.opinion: A lighthearted satirical piece poking fun at the AI industry's search for compelling consumer use cases.

tweet_headlines.author: mardehaym
tweet_headlines.headline: Think a restaurant menu, not a slide deck: this agency's __20-dish AI services pitch__ lists the exact metric each workflow moves instead of a price.
tweet_headlines.source_text:
Nobody reads a standard AI services deck.

So we turned ours into a menu.

20 dishes. Each one is an operational bottleneck AI takes off your team's plate, such as closing the books, chasing overdue invoices, fielding inbound calls, or quoting a custom part.

Where a traditional menu prints the price, ours prints the exact metric the dish moves: Days to close. Quote turnaround. Days sales outstanding.

Every dish also carries a single proof line. It’s either a production build we’ve shipped or a named 2026 case from another company, clearly labeled so you know which is which.

The Courses:
> Starters: Quick wins, like workspace automations and document intake.
> Mains: Core operations: the close, billing, quoting, and the ERP.
> For the table: Revenue and customer-facing workflows: pipeline, pricing, and support.
> Sector specials: Industry-specific compliance and operations, including KYC, insurance claims, and AML.
> Chef’s specials: Custom production agents we’ve already shipped, such as RCM billing and automated code review.

How to order: Pick one team and one dish. 

We baseline the target metric before writing a single line of code, and a human verifies every output throughout the pilot.

All three pages are below. 

Which dish are you ordering first?

tweet_headlines.author: damkina7
tweet_headlines.headline: One settings change in Claude Code assigns each model a role: __Opus 5.5 plans, Sonnet 5.5 builds, Fable 5.2 tears your diff apart__.
tweet_headlines.source_text:
i still can't comprehend why senior engineers run claude code on default configuration.

one settings change and every model gets its own job:

→ opus 5.5 architects every plan and unblocks when stuck
→ sonnet 5.5 writes the production code
→ haiku scouts file paths and line numbers with zero overhead
→ fable 5.2 tears your diff apart before you merge

Opus thinks. Sonnet builds. Fable attacks. Haiku scouts.

paste this into claude code ↓

Add this to ~/.claude/settings.json. Keep every hook, permission and plugin I already have. Then create the two agent files below and show me the diff.

```json
{
  "model": "opusplan",
  "advisorModel": "opus",
  "effortLevel": "medium",
  "modelSettings": {
    "claude-opus-5-5": { "effortLevel": "high" },
    "claude-sonnet-5-5": { "effortLevel": "medium" },
    "claude-fable-5-2": { "effortLevel": "high" }
  },
  "env": {
    "CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL": "haiku"
  }
}
```

~/.claude/agents/scout.md
```
---
name: scout
description: finds code fast. returns file paths and line numbers only.
model: haiku
tools: Read, Grep, Glob
---
Locate exactly what was asked. Return file:line. No fixes. No opinions.
```

~/.claude/agents/critic.md
```
---
name: critic
description: reviews a diff or plan before any task is called done
model: fable-5-2
tools: Read, Grep, Bash
---
Assume this is broken. Find how it fails. One line per issue, worst first.
```

tweet_headlines.author: noahkagan
tweet_headlines.headline: Noah Kagan let Claude audit AppSumo's support inbox over a weekend and found __1,298 tickets in 33 days__ — 30% self-generated by their own automated emails.
tweet_headlines.source_text:
I told Claude to work the weekend! 

Copy this prompt:
"I'm not working this weekend. You are. Figure out what matters most at {your company}. Surprise me Monday with the results."

Its pick: our partner support inbox. That's the founders who sell their software on AppSumo. 🥁

1,298 tickets in 33 days.

What it found:

- 30% were partners replying to our own automated emails
- 117 were replies to ONE rejection email
- 16% weren't partners at all. Spam, newsletters, lost buyers.
- Our "Go to support" link pointed to the wrong page
- The FAQ was out of date and in no order

We were creating our own tickets. 🤦

The fixes:

1- Stop nudging partners about things they already did
2- Show them where their submission stands
3- Tell rejected partners they can reapply in 30 days
4- Move the noise out of the inbox

I spent a day updating its fixes.

Partner tickets: 60 a day → 15.

Ask Claude to work this weekend for you, let me know what it suggests!

tweet_headlines.author: noahkagan
tweet_headlines.headline: An agent-written changelog took AppSumo from __60 to 3,437 Google impressions in 3 weeks__ — Noah Kagan shares the Claude Code prompt.
tweet_headlines.source_text:
Steal this SEO move. Changelogs. 📈

Our changelog page went from 60 Google impressions to 3,437 in 3 weeks. 📈

TidyCal (our scheduling app) put up a dated changelog page and kept adding to it.

A page that changes every week gives Google a reason to come back. Most of your site never changes. 

It also pushes notifications so customers see every update. 

Now an agent writes it every Friday. Paste this into Claude Code with GitHub connected:

"Every Friday, check everything we merged on GitHub. Skip internal fixes. For each new feature or change a customer would notice, write one line in plain words: what changed, why it's valuable to them, and a link to it if there is one. Put today's date on top. Add the entry to /changelog, newest on top."

Same page, updated every week, no one has to remember.

Connect GitHub and run it this Friday.

tweet_headlines.author: WasimShips
tweet_headlines.headline: WasimShips's __mobile UI system__ drops flat fills for layered shadows, Inter Tight throughout, negative tracking on every heading.
tweet_headlines.source_text:
Steal this clean mobile app UI system :  

- Titles: Inter Tight 22/28px Semi Bold, 
-0.7px letter spacing
 - Section headers: Inter Tight 19/24px Semi Bold, and 0.6px letter spacing 
- Body/day labels: Inter Tight 14.5/18px Regular, and 0.3px letter spacing 
- Buttons: 38-46px circular, 6px inset highlight + soft drop shadow, no flat fills 
- Cards: 12-18px radius depending on depth, layered box-shadows not borders 
- Text: var(--text) for primary, var(--muted) for secondary, var(--strong) for icons 
- Dividers: 1px var(--track), never a visible border color 

Tight tokens, layered shadows instead of borders, negative tracking on every heading.   

That's what makes dense mobile screens still feel calm.
